Adding ops notes from initial telemetry:
- Observed a sudden increase in KV cache evictions correlated with the spike at 08:53 PT. Cache miss rate jumped ~6x.
- A recent routing config (auto-scale policy bump) experienced a delayed pod spin-up during the surge window.
- 5xxs are coming from model-inference nodes returning OOM/timeout errors under peak batch sizes.

Immediate actions in progress:
- Scaling policy override to increase burst capacity (rolling now).
- Temporarily disable aggressive batching for the checkout model to reduce tail latency.
- Collecting full diag bundle: diag-logs.tar.gz (attaching).

Will update in the war-room.

—Marissa

Team / Raj — quick executive summary for leadership and the customer execs:
- Impact: Checkout latency (p95) increased from 220ms to ~650ms; sustained 5xx ~7% for 15m window. Estimated revenue impact: high for checkout-heavy traffic windows.
- Root signals: fast-growing KV eviction + delayed autoscale during burst => increased batch sizes leading to model OOM/timeouts.
- Immediate mitigations: increased burst pool, disabled aggressive batching, emergency KV cache policy tweak. Observed partial recovery starting 09:58 PT.

Request: please confirm availability for a 30-minute exec check-in at 11:30 PT to review remediation, customer-facing timeline, and credit/contract implications.

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 12:47:00 -0800
Subject: Northstar — post-mitigation readout and next steps

Team / Raj — final summary from today's incident and immediate next steps.

What we saw:
- Instant spike at 08:53 PT driven by cache thrash + concurrent burst where autoscale did not provision capacity quickly enough.
- Batch-size growth on inference nodes pushed a subset of model pods into OOM/timeouts, producing the 5xxs.

What we did (chronological):
- 09:00: increased burst pool and forced additional GPU capacity;
- 09:02: disabled aggressive batching for affected model;
- 09:10: applied KV cache policy change to reduce eviction churn;
- 09:25–09:40: monitored steady state; observed errors drop from 7% -> 0.6% and p95 latency return to 240ms.

Customer impact: checkout success rate returned to baseline by 10:05 PT; ongoing monitoring shows steady SLO adherence (>95% of requests within targets).

Post-incident actions (owners):
- Runbook update: autoscale policy guardrails + explicit burst warmup (Marissa will draft) — owner: Marissa Cole.
- SLO/credits review: finance/sales to propose a customer goodwill package (Kimberly) — owner: Kimberly Park.
- Postmortem + customer timing: draft postmortem by EOD Monday, internal review Tuesday, customer-facing summary after legal/CS review — owner: David Kim. Attachment: postmortem-draft.docx

Thanks to everyone who jumped in. Raj, we will cover the customer-facing note in the 11:30 call (recording will be shared).

David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
